verses.1:1: Paul, an apostle of Jesus Christ through the will of God, to all the saints who are at Ephesus, and to the faithful in Christ Jesus.
verses.1:2: Grace to you, and peace from God our Father and from the Lord Jesus Christ.
verses.1:3: Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who blessed us in every spiritual blessing in the heavenly places in Christ,
verses.1:4: just as He chose us in Him before the founding of the world, that we might be holy and unblemished in His sight in love.
verses.1:5: He predestined us for adoption as sons through Jesus Christ to Himself, according to the purpose of His will,
verses.1:6: to the praise of the glory of His grace, in which He favored us in His beloved Son.
verses.1:7: In Him we have redemption through His blood, the forgiveness of sins, according to the riches of His grace,
verses.1:8: which abounded exceedingly in us in all wisdom and insight,
verses.1:9: so that He might make known to us the mystery of His will, according to His good pleasure, which He purposed in Him,
verses.1:10: in the administration of the fullness of times, to restore all things in Christ, the things that are in the heavens and the things that are on earth, in Him;
verses.1:11: in whom we also were called by lot, having been predestined according to the purpose of the One who works all things according to the counsel of His will,
verses.1:12: so that we might be to the praise of His glory, we who hoped beforehand in Christ;
verses.1:13: in whom you also, when you had heard the word of truth, the Gospel of your salvation, in whom also, believing, you were sealed with the Holy Spirit of promise,
verses.1:14: who is the pledge of our inheritance, for the redemption of the acquisition, to the praise of His glory.
verses.1:15: For this reason I also, hearing of your faith that is in the Lord Jesus and love toward all the saints,
verses.1:16: do not cease giving thanks for you, making remembrance of you in my prayers,
verses.1:17: that the God of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of glory, may grant you a spirit of wisdom and revelation in the knowledge of Him,
verses.1:18: with the eyes of your heart enlightened, so that you may know what is the hope of His calling, and what are the riches of the glory of His inheritance in the saints,
verses.1:19: and what is the surpassing greatness of His power toward us who believe, according to the working of the might of His power,
verses.1:20: which He worked in Christ, raising Him from the dead and setting Him at His right hand in the heavenly places,
verses.1:21: above every principality and authority and power and dominion, and every name that is named, not only in this age, but also in the future one.
verses.1:22: And He subjected all things under His feet, and gave Him as head over the whole church,
verses.1:23: which is His body, and the fullness of the One who is filled all in all.
verses.2:1: And you, when you were dead in your offenses and sins,
verses.2:2: in which you once walked according to the age of this world, according to the prince of the authority of this air, of the spirit that now works in the sons of unbelief,
verses.2:3: among whom we all also once lived in the desires of our flesh, doing the will of the flesh and of the thoughts, and were by nature sons of wrath, just as the rest also;
verses.2:4: but God, who is rich in mercy, because of His exceeding love with which He loved us,
verses.2:5: even when we were dead in sins, made us alive together in Christ (by whose grace you have been saved),
verses.2:6: and raised us up together, and made us sit together in the heavenly places in Christ Jesus,
verses.2:7: so that He might show in the coming ages the abundant riches of His grace, in goodness toward us in Christ Jesus.
verses.2:8: For by grace you have been saved through faith, and this is not from yourselves, for it is God's gift,
verses.2:9: not from works, so that no one may boast.
verses.2:10: For we are His handiwork, created in Christ Jesus in good works, which God prepared so that we might walk in them.
verses.2:11: Therefore remember that once you, Gentiles in the flesh, who are called uncircumcision by that which is called circumcision in the flesh, made by hand,
verses.2:12: that at that time you were without Christ, alienated from the citizenship of Israel and strangers to the covenants, having no hope of the promise, and without God in this world.
verses.2:13: But now in Christ Jesus, you who once were far off have been made near in the blood of Christ.
verses.2:14: For He Himself is our peace, who made both one, and breaking down the dividing wall of partition, the hostilities in His flesh,
verses.2:15: nullifying the law of commandments by decrees, so that He might create the two in Himself into one new man, making peace,
verses.2:16: and might reconcile both in one body to God through the cross, putting to death the hostilities in Himself.
verses.2:17: And coming, He proclaimed the good news of peace to you who were far off, and peace to those who were near.
verses.2:18: For through Him both of us have access in one Spirit to the Father.
verses.2:19: So then you are no longer strangers and sojourners, but you are citizens with the saints and members of God's household,
verses.2:20: built upon the foundation of the apostles and prophets, with Christ Jesus Himself as the chief cornerstone,
verses.2:21: in whom the entire building, assembled together, grows into a holy temple in the Lord,
verses.2:22: in whom you also are being built together into a dwelling place of God in the Spirit.
verses.3:1: For this reason, I, Paul, the prisoner of Christ Jesus on behalf of you Gentiles,
verses.3:2: if indeed you have heard of the administration of the grace of God, which was given to me among you,
verses.3:3: that according to revelation the mystery was made known to me, just as I wrote above in brief,
verses.3:4: as you are able, when reading, to understand my insight into the mystery of Christ,
verses.3:5: which in other generations was not known to the sons of men, as it has now been revealed to His holy apostles and prophets in the Spirit,
verses.3:6: that the Gentiles are co-heirs, and of the same body, and joint partakers of His promise in Christ Jesus through the Gospel,
verses.3:7: of which I became a minister according to the gift of the grace of God, which was given to me according to the working of His power.
verses.3:8: To me, the least of all the saints, this grace was given, to proclaim among the Gentiles the good news of the unsearchable riches of Christ,
verses.3:9: and to enlighten all as to what is the administration of the mystery hidden from the ages in God, who created all things,
verses.3:10: so that the manifold wisdom of God might become known through the church to the principalities and authorities in the heavenly places,
verses.3:11: according to the predetermination of the ages, which He carried out in Christ Jesus our Lord,
verses.3:12: in whom we have boldness and access in confidence through faith in Him.
verses.3:13: Therefore I ask that you do not lose heart in my tribulations for you, which is your glory.
verses.3:14: For this reason I bend my knees to the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ,
verses.3:15: from whom every fatherhood in the heavens and on earth is named,
verses.3:16: that He may grant you, according to the riches of His glory, to be strengthened with power through His Spirit in the inner man,
verses.3:17: for Christ to dwell through faith in your hearts, rooted and founded in love,
verses.3:18: so that you may be able to comprehend with all the saints what is the width and length and height and depth,
verses.3:19: and to know also the love of Christ, surpassing knowledge, so that you may be filled to all the fullness of God.
verses.3:20: Now to Him who is able to do all things far more abundantly than we ask or understand, according to the power that works in us,
verses.3:21: to Him be glory in the church and in Christ Jesus throughout all generations of the age of ages. Amen.
verses.4:1: Therefore I, a prisoner in the Lord, implore you to walk worthily of the calling by which you were called,
verses.4:2: with all humility and meekness, with patience, bearing with one another in love,
verses.4:3: careful to preserve the unity of the Spirit in the bond of peace.
verses.4:4: One body and one Spirit, just as you were called in one hope of your calling.
verses.4:5: One Lord, one faith, one baptism.
verses.4:6: One God and Father of all, who is above all, and through all things, and in all of us.
verses.4:7: Now to each one of us grace was given according to the measure of the gift of Christ.
verses.4:8: For this reason it says: "Ascending on high, He led captivity captive; He gave gifts to people."
verses.4:9: Now what does it mean that He ascended, except that He also first descended into the lower parts of the earth?
verses.4:10: He who descended is Himself also He who ascended above all the heavens, so that He might fill all things.
verses.4:11: And He Himself gave some to be apostles, some prophets, others evangelists, and still others pastors and teachers,
verses.4:12: for the completion of the saints, for the work of ministry, for the building up of the body of Christ,
verses.4:13: until we all arrive at the unity of the faith and of the knowledge of the Son of God, to a perfect man, to the measure of the age of the fullness of Christ,
verses.4:14: so that we may no longer be little children tossed by waves and carried about by every wind of teaching, in the wickedness of people, in craftiness for the scheming of error.
verses.4:15: Instead, doing the truth in love, let us grow in Him in all things, who is the head, Christ,
verses.4:16: from whom the whole body, fitted and joined together through every joint of supply, according to the working in the measure of each individual member, produces the growth of the body for the building up of itself in love.
verses.4:17: Therefore I say this and testify in the Lord, that you should no longer walk just as the Gentiles also walk, in the futility of their thinking,
verses.4:18: having their understanding obscured by darkness, alienated from the life of God through the ignorance that is in them, because of the blindness of their heart,
verses.4:19: who, despairing, handed themselves over to shamelessness, for the working of all impurity in greed.
verses.4:20: You, however, did not learn Christ in such a way,
verses.4:21: if indeed you heard Him and were instructed in Him, just as truth is in Jesus:
verses.4:22: that you put off, according to the former way of life, the old man, who is being corrupted according to the desires of error.
verses.4:23: But be renewed in the spirit of your mind,
verses.4:24: and put on the new man, who was created according to God in righteousness and holiness of truth.
verses.4:25: For this reason, putting off lying, speak truth, each one with his neighbor, because we are members of one another.
verses.4:26: Be angry, and do not sin; let the sun not set upon your anger.
verses.4:27: Do not give room to the devil.
verses.4:28: Let the one who used to steal steal no longer; rather, let him labor, doing with his own hands what is good, so that he may have the means to give to the one suffering need.
verses.4:29: Let no evil speech proceed from your mouth, but whatever is good for the building up of faith, so that it may give grace to those who hear.
verses.4:30: And do not sadden the Holy Spirit of God, in whom you were sealed for the day of redemption.
verses.4:31: Let all bitterness, and wrath, and indignation, and shouting, and slander be removed from you, along with all malice.
verses.4:32: But be kind to one another, merciful, forgiving one another, just as God in Christ also forgave you.
verses.5:1: Be imitators of God, therefore, as most beloved children,
verses.5:2: and walk in love, just as Christ also loved us and delivered Himself up for us, an offering and a sacrifice to God for an aroma of sweetness.
verses.5:3: But fornication and all impurity or greed must not even be named among you, as is fitting for saints,
verses.5:4: nor obscenity, nor foolish talk, nor vulgar joking, which is out of place, but rather thanksgiving.
verses.5:5: For know this, understanding that no fornicator, or impure, or greedy person, which is the service of idols, has an inheritance in the kingdom of Christ and God.
verses.5:6: Let no one mislead you with empty words, for because of these things the wrath of God comes upon the sons of unbelief.
verses.5:7: Therefore do not become sharers with them.
verses.5:8: For once you were darkness, but now light in the Lord. Walk as children of light,
verses.5:9: for the fruit of light is in all goodness, and righteousness, and truth,
verses.5:10: discerning what is well-pleasing to God,
verses.5:11: and do not share in the fruitless works of darkness, but rather expose them.
verses.5:12: For the things done in secret by them are shameful even to speak of.
verses.5:13: But all things that are exposed are revealed by the light; for everything that is revealed is light.
verses.5:14: For this reason it says: "Rise, you who sleep, and rise up from the dead, and Christ will give you light."
verses.5:15: See therefore, brothers, how carefully you walk, not as unwise,
verses.5:16: but as wise, redeeming the time, since the days are evil.
verses.5:17: Because of this, do not become foolish, but understand what the will of God is.
verses.5:18: And do not become drunk with wine, in which there is debauchery, but be filled with the Holy Spirit,
verses.5:19: speaking to yourselves in psalms, and hymns, and spiritual songs, singing and making music in your hearts to the Lord,
verses.5:20: giving thanks always for all things in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ to God and the Father,
verses.5:21: subject to one another in the fear of Christ.
verses.5:22: Let wives be subject to their own husbands, as to the Lord,
verses.5:23: because the husband is the head of the wife, just as Christ is the head of the church; He Himself is the Savior of His body.
verses.5:24: But just as the church is subject to Christ, so also let wives be to their husbands in everything.
verses.5:25: Husbands, love your wives, just as Christ also loved the church and delivered Himself up for her,
verses.5:26: so that He might sanctify her, cleansing her by the washing of water in the word of life,
verses.5:27: so that He Himself might present to Himself a glorious church, not having spot, or wrinkle, or anything of this kind, but so that she may be holy and spotless.
verses.5:28: So also husbands ought to love their wives as their own bodies. The one who loves his own wife loves himself.
verses.5:29: For no one has ever hated his own flesh, but feeds and cherishes it, just as Christ also does the church,
verses.5:30: because we are members of His body, of His flesh and of His bones.
verses.5:31: Because of this, a man will leave his father and his mother and will cling to his wife, and the two will be in one flesh.
verses.5:32: This mystery is great; I, however, speak in Christ and in the church.
verses.5:33: Nevertheless, you also individually, let each one love his own wife as himself; and let the wife fear her husband.
verses.6:1: Children, obey your parents in the Lord, because this is right.
verses.6:2: "Honor your father and your mother," which is the first commandment with a promise:
verses.6:3: "so that it may go well with you, and you may be long-lived on the earth."
verses.6:4: And you, fathers, do not provoke your children to anger, but raise them in the discipline and correction of the Lord.
verses.6:5: Slaves, obey your masters in the flesh with fear and trembling, in the sincerity of your heart, as to Christ,
verses.6:6: not serving to the eye, as though pleasing people, but as slaves of Christ, doing the will of God from the soul,
verses.6:7: serving with good will, as to the Lord and not to people,
verses.6:8: knowing that each one, whatever good he has done, will receive this from the Lord, whether slave or free.
verses.6:9: And you, masters, do the same things to them, giving up threats, knowing that both their Lord and yours is in heaven, and there is no partiality with Him.
verses.6:10: Finally, brothers, be strengthened in the Lord and in the power of His strength.
verses.6:11: Put on the armor of God, so that you may be able to stand against the plots of the devil,
verses.6:12: for our wrestling is not against flesh and blood, but against rulers and authorities, against the world rulers of this darkness, against the spiritual forces of wickedness in the heavenly places.
verses.6:13: Therefore, take up the armor of God, so that you may be able to resist in the evil day and to stand perfected in all things.
verses.6:14: Stand, therefore, with your waist belted in truth, and having put on the breastplate of righteousness,
verses.6:15: and with your feet fitted in the preparation of the gospel of peace,
verses.6:16: in all things taking up the shield of faith, with which you may be able to extinguish all the flaming arrows of the most wicked one;
verses.6:17: and receive the helmet of salvation, and the sword of the Spirit (which is the word of God),
verses.6:18: through all prayer and petition, praying at all times in the Spirit, and keeping watch in it with all persistence and petition for all the saints,
verses.6:19: and for me, that speech may be given to me in the opening of my mouth with boldness, to make known the mystery of the gospel,
verses.6:20: for which I serve as an ambassador in a chain, so that in it I may be bold, just as I ought to speak.
verses.6:21: Now so that you also may know the things concerning me, what I am doing, Tychicus, dearest brother and faithful minister in the Lord, will make all things known to you.
verses.6:22: I have sent him to you for this very reason, so that you may come to know the things concerning us, and that he may comfort your hearts.
verses.6:23: Peace to the brothers, and love with faith, from God the Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
verses.6:24: Grace be with all who love our Lord Jesus Christ in incorruptibility. Amen.

notes.1:4: In the Clementine Vulgate, "in love" (in caritate) closes verse 4 rather than introducing verse 5, which begins a new sentence (Qui praedestinavit).
notes.1:6: The Vulgate adds Filio ("in His beloved Son"), whereas Greek reads simply "in the Beloved."
notes.1:10: Latin instaurare literally means "to restore" or "renew," a distinctive Vulgate rendering where Greek uses a verb meaning "to sum up" or "bring together under one head."
notes.1:22: Latin supra omnem ecclesiam means "over the whole church" (with feminine omnem modifying ecclesiam), whereas Greek reads "head over all things to the church."
notes.1:23: Latin adimpletur is passive in form ("is filled"); the Vulgate also includes "and" (et) before "the fullness."
notes.2:2: The Vulgate adds hujus ("this air") and renders the final phrase filios diffidentiae, literally "sons of unbelief" or "distrust" (where Greek has "disobedience").
notes.2:5: The Vulgate reads in Christo ("in Christ," rather than "with Christ") and adds the relative pronoun cujus ("by whose grace you have been saved") in the parenthetical clause.
notes.2:8: The Vulgate includes a second enim ("for") in Dei enim donum est ("for it is God's gift").
notes.2:12: Clementine Vulgate punctuation attaches promissionis to spem ("having no hope of the promise") rather than to testamentorum ("covenants"), and adds hoc ("in this world").
notes.2:15: Latin decretis is an unadorned ablative ("by decrees"), which Latin interpreters have understood either instrumentally (nullifying the law through Christ's decrees) or descriptively (the law consisting in decrees).
notes.3:3: The Vulgate uses sacramentum ("sacred secret" or "mystery") here and in 1:9 and 3:9, alternating with mysterium in 3:4 to denote the same hidden divine plan.
notes.3:11: Latin praefinitionem saeculorum literally means "predetermination of the ages."
notes.3:12: Latin 'per fidem ejus' literally reads 'through the faith of Him,' understood here objectively ('through faith in Him'), though it can also be read subjectively ('through His faithfulness').
notes.3:14: The Vulgate includes "of our Lord Jesus Christ" (Domini nostri Jesu Christi) after "the Father," a reading absent from some Greek manuscripts.
notes.3:15: Latin paternitas literally means "fatherhood" (preserving the wordplay with Patrem, "Father," in verse 14), whereas Greek patria denotes "family" or "lineage."
notes.3:20: Latin omnia facere superabundanter quam makes "all things" (omnia) the direct object of "do," and intelligimus specifically means "understand" (where Greek has "think").
notes.4:6: The Clementine Vulgate reads "in all of us" (in omnibus nobis), whereas the critical Greek text has simply "in all" (and some later Greek manuscripts read "in you all").
notes.4:14: The Vulgate renders the Greek term for "trickery" or "dice-playing" more broadly as "wickedness" (nequitia).
notes.4:15: Where the Greek reads "speaking/maintaining the truth" (aletheuontes), the Vulgate literally has "doing the truth" (veritatem facientes).
notes.4:19: The Vulgate renders Greek "having become callous" as "despairing" (desperantes, reflecting a reading meaning "having lost hope"); similarly, in 4:18 it translates Greek "hardness" as "blindness" (caecitatem).
notes.4:23: Latin bare ablative 'spiritu mentis vestræ' ("in the spirit of your mind") has no preposition and can be understood either locatively of the renewed human inner spirit ("in the spirit of your mind") or instrumentally of the divine Spirit ("by the Spirit of your mind").
notes.4:29: The Vulgate reads "for the building up of faith" (ad aedificationem fidei), following an ancient textual variant where the critical Greek text reads "of the need" (as fits the occasion).
notes.5:5: The Vulgate reads "which is the service of idols" (quod est idolorum servitus, i.e., idolatry), where the critical Greek text has masculine "who is an idolater."
notes.5:15: The Clementine Vulgate adds the address "brothers" (fratres), absent from standard Greek texts; similarly, it specifies "to God" (5:10) and "the will of God" (5:17) where Greek has "the Lord," and "the Holy Spirit" (5:18) where Greek has simply "the Spirit."
notes.5:26: The Clementine Vulgate adds "of life" (in verbo vitae, "in the word of life"), whereas the Greek text reads simply "in the word."
notes.5:30: The Vulgate includes "of His flesh and of His bones" (de carne ejus et de ossibus ejus), a reading found in many ancient witnesses but omitted in the critical Greek text.
notes.5:32: Latin sacramentum, the Vulgate's usual equivalent of Greek mysterion, is rendered "mystery" here as in 1:9, 3:3 and 3:9; "in Christ and in the church" literally renders in Christo et in Ecclesia, meaning with reference to Christ and the church.
notes.6:10: The Clementine Vulgate includes fratres ('brothers'), which is omitted in many modern critical Greek editions (while the Textus Receptus reads 'my brothers').
notes.6:13: The Vulgate reading in omnibus perfecti stare ('to stand perfected in all things') differs from the Greek text, which reads 'having done everything, to stand.'
notes.6:16: Latin nequissimi is superlative ('the most wicked one'), rendering the positive Greek phrase 'the evil one'; in omnibus ('in all things') reflects the Greek reading en pasin rather than epi pasin ('above all').
notes.6:18: Latin in ipso ('in it') refers to prayer, though grammatically in Latin it can also mean 'in Him,' referring back to the Spirit.
notes.6:24: Latin in incorruptione ('in incorruptibility') is often understood as referring to unfailing or imperishable love; the Clementine Vulgate also retains 'Amen,' which is omitted in many modern Greek editions.
